slots.title: September job openings 7.5M beat 7.1M estimate
slots.body:
September U.S. job openings: 7.5M (JOLTS).

Consensus: 7.1M.

Prior month (August): 7.19M.

The print landed the same day voters cast midterm ballots, with coverage tying stronger postings to employers hiring into firmer growth — while many households still report pressure from higher prices.

Quits also ran above forecast: 3.4M vs 3.05M expected (August: 3.04M).

What part of the labor picture do you watch first — openings, quits, or tomorrow’s ADP print?

slots.title: US session recap — Nov. 3, 2026
slots.body:
The Nasdaq Composite led U.S. equity indexes, closing up 0.8% at 25,372.01.
The S&P 500 rose 0.4% to 7,568.71.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished down 0.4% at 51,786.72, and the Russell 2000 added 0.2% to 2,812.45.

Tuesday was U.S. midterm election day, and headlines described early political momentum alongside mixed index performance.

At 3 p.m.
Eastern, JOLTs job openings for September printed at 7.523 million, above the 7.1 million estimate and prior 7.19 million.
Durable goods orders ex transportation rose 0.5% month over month, in line with the estimate.

The CBOE Volatility Index fell 1.5% to 20.83, with an intraday range of 20.29 to 21.91.

On Nasdaq sector averages, Industrials led at about +1.7%, followed by Real Estate about +1.5%, Utilities about +1.2%, and Technology about +0.8%.
Basic Materials lagged at about -1.5%, and Consumer Defensive was about -1.2%.

Advanced Micro Devices rose 3.7% to 483.90 after EPS of 2.09 on revenue of about $13.38 billion, both above estimates.
NVIDIA gained 2.3% to 206.69.
Amazon.com rose 2.1% to 250.69.
Arista Networks added 3.5% to 169.91 after an earnings beat.
ASML gained 1.7% to 1,552.14.

Apollo Global Management fell 4.9% to 113.55 after revenue of about $4.74 billion missed a much higher estimate.
Keurig Dr Pepper dropped 5.6% to 34.74 despite an EPS beat.
Pfizer declined 2.2% to 30.00 after beating on EPS and revenue.

Gold futures rose 0.3% to 3,953.30.
The United States Oil Fund (WTI proxy) gained 0.8% to 158.17, while Brent crude fell 0.7% to 102.87.
The dollar-bullish fund proxy (UUP) ticked up 0.2% to 29.01.
Bitcoin slipped 0.3% to 77,136.54.

Overseas, Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell 4.7% to 60,089.56.
The FTSE 100 lost 1.1% to 10,638.43.

Latest Treasury snapshot in the feed (Oct. 30) showed the 10-year at 4.9% and the 2s10s spread at 0.38 percentage point.

slots.title: October jobs report due Friday at 8:30 a.m.
slots.body:
Nonfarm payrolls for October are scheduled for Friday, Nov. 6, at 8:30 a.m.
ET (13:30 in the calendar feed).

The median estimate is 65K jobs added, versus 29K in the prior month’s print.

The unemployment rate is expected at 4.2%, unchanged from September.

Average hourly earnings are expected up 0.3% month over month and 2.9% year over year.

Private payrolls are also pegged at 65K; the broader report includes government and manufacturing breakdowns in the same release.

That bundle is the main US labor read for the week and closes the window on October hiring.

Which line in the report do you usually read first—headline jobs, unemployment, or wages?

slots.title: Jobless claims and productivity hit Thursday 8:30
slots.body:
Two labor-market prints share the Thursday, Nov. 5, 8:30 a.m.
ET slot.

Initial jobless claims (Oct/31): estimate 196K, prior 194K.

Jobless claims 4-week average: estimate 196K, prior 196.75K.

Continuing claims (Oct/24): estimate 1,710K, prior 1,701K.

Nonfarm productivity QoQ (Q3): estimate 2.5%, prior 1.4%.

Claims track layoff pace near term; productivity measures output per hour and feeds into how firms are using labor.

Results drop two days before the October payrolls report.

Do you treat weekly claims as a leading hint for the monthly jobs number or as noise?
